summary: Elevated initial response latency for chat completions after inference compiler swap and model handoff
description: Customer reports increased delay before first token on streaming chat responses after a scheduled compiler/runtime swap and model variant handoff. Impact: user-facing chat features intermittently stall ~0.6-1.2s before the first chunk appears, and some requests surface 504 timeouts when streaming is enabled.
steps_to_reproduce: Start an interactive chat session using the completions streaming API with model pinned to gptx-13b-v2.
Send an initial prompt of ~30 tokens (e.g., 'Draft a two-paragraph product summary').
Observe time from request to first stream chunk; compare against baseline (expected ~<150ms).
Repeat across multiple sessions on us-west-2 and track percentiles.
Run curl with stream=true and request timeout 10s to reproduce 504s on some requests.

investigation_notes: Spike correlates with 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC rollout of runtime compiler v2.9.0 and automated handoff to quantized variant on traffic-shaping policy.
Early signal: queue_wait_ms jumped on affected requests suggesting scheduling/batching policy changed kernel selection path.
Cache warm-up missing: many requests show kv_warm=false causing additional prefix recomputation overhead.
Hypothesis A: kernel selector now prefers fallback path that triggers a small compatibility shim adding ~400-700ms to first-chunk path.
Hypothesis B: continuous batching window configured higher in new compiler causing added queuing for low-concurrency chat sessions.
Eng traced a hot path in runtime where kernel loading on first invocation for V2.9 pulls extra CPU-bound initialization.
No evidence of GPU starvation or node OOMs in CloudWatch during incident window.
actions_taken: Rolled back scheduled canary of compiler v2.9.0 on us-west-2 autoscaling group at 2026-03-10T03:05Z.
Applied temporary routing rule to prefer fp16 variant for latency-sensitive customer traffic.
Increased batching timeout threshold down to 3ms for small chat queues as a short-term mitigation.
Opened runtime PR to add async kernel prefetch for quantized variants (PR #827).
resolution: Mitigation reduced median first-chunk latency for NimbleAI from ~650ms to ~130ms; 95p decreased from 1.2s to 240ms after rollback and routing change.
Follow-up: runtime team will ship kernel prefetch and explicit kv-cache priming in v2.9.1; scheduled for 2026-03-17 rollout behind canary with telemetry flags.
Customer notified and will validate in their staging environment before gradual re-enablement.
Close criteria: stable 95p first-chunk <350ms for 24h on their traffic pattern in us-west-2.
